questions.question: Explain what scale is and why maps must be drawn to scale.
questions.expected_answer: Scale is the relationship between a distance on a map and the real distance on the ground, and it tells us how many times smaller the map is than the real world. Maps must be drawn to scale because the real world is far too big to show at its real size, and shrinking everything by the same amount keeps shapes and distances correct.

questions.question: Explain the difference between a large-scale map and a small-scale map and give an example of each.
questions.expected_answer: A large-scale map shows a small area, such as a few streets or a town, in a lot of detail, for example a street map. A small-scale map shows a large area, such as a country, a continent or the world, in little detail, for example a world map in an atlas.

questions.question: Which map would you use to find a house in your suburb, and which to plan a journey across Africa? Explain why.
questions.expected_answer: To find a house, use a large-scale street map, because it shows a small area with streets and buildings in detail. To plan a journey across Africa, use a small-scale map of Africa, because it shows the whole large area with countries, big roads and cities.
